glosses: to sprinkle, asperse
обрызгивать

examples.text: У соседних изб с вёдрами воды стояли бабы и девки, кропили стены мокрыми вениками, сбивали и тушили огненные хлопья.
Он кропил шашлыки жёлтым уксусом из одной бутылки, красным перцем из другой, засыпал рубленым луком и совал подручному.

glosses: религ. обрызгивать освящённой водой (при совершении некоторых христианских обрядов)

examples.text: А преосвященнейший Амвросий, идучи с крестом, кропил святою водою по обе стороны.

glosses: неперех. падать мелкими каплями; накрапывать (о дожде)

examples.text: Дождь кропил, серое, хмурое небо сократило горизонт до крайности.

glosses: To sprinkle.

examples.text: At this crisis the Sabine women, from the outrage on whom the war had arisen, with dishevelled hair and torn garments, the timidity natural to women being overcome by the sense of their calamities, were emboldened to fling themselves into the midst of the flying weapons, and, rushing across, to part the incensed combatants and assuage their wrath: imploring their fathers on the one hand and their husbands on the other, as fathers-in-law and sons-in-law, not to besprinkle themselves with impious blood, nor to fix the stain of murder on their offspring, the one side on their grandchildren, the other on their children.

We could still recognize the troughs that served for the manipulation of the bread, and the oven, the arch of which is intact, with the cavity that retained the ashes, the vase for water to besprinkle the crust and make it shiny, and, finally, the triple-flued pipe that carried off the smoke — an excellent system revealed by the Pompeian excavations and successfully imitated since then.

glosses: To cause (a substance) to fall in fine drops (for a liquid substance) or small pieces (for a solid substance).

examples.text: The confectioner sprinkled icing sugar over the cakes.
And the priest shall[…]sprinkle of the oil with his finger seven times before the Lord.

At twilight in the summer[…]the mice come out. They[…]eat the luncheon crumbs. Mr. Checkly, for instance, always brought his dinner in a paper parcel in his coat-tail pocket, and ate it when so disposed, sprinkling crumbs lavishly[…]on the floor.
Over the centuries the movement of clans and tribes of people has provided the kind of crop that would emerge if a blind god had sprinkled seeds at random on a field[.]

glosses: To cover (an object) by sprinkling a substance on to it.

examples.text: The confectioner sprinkled the cakes with icing sugar.

Most of the passengers watched from the enclosed promenade deck, but Sandra found her way to the higher, open promenade where she shivered and watched the city lights fade and the stars sprinkle themselves across a dark blue velvet sky.

glosses: To drip in fine drops, sometimes sporadically.

examples.text: It sprinkled outside all day long.

glosses: To rain very lightly outside.

examples.text: It sprinkled very early in the morning.

glosses: To baptize by the application of a few drops, or a small quantity, of water; hence, to cleanse; to purify.

examples.text: having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience

glosses: A light covering with a sprinkled substance.

examples.text: He decorated the Christmas card with a sprinkle of glitter.
My memory leaves me with a constant and deep burning, my eyes stinging and red from short sprinkles of tears which have been sneaking up on me for days now.

glosses: A light rain shower.
An aspersorium or utensil for sprinkling.
A small hard piece of sugar and starch, or chocolate, used to decorate cakes etc.
To sprinkle or scatter (liquid or dust).

examples.text: a hand in San Marco's font / aspersed him with foul canal water

glosses: To falsely or maliciously charge someone.

examples.text: It hath always been my way to baffle reproach with silence; though I cannot but observe the disingenuous proceedings of this gentleman, who is not content to asperse my writings, but hath wounded, through my sides, those eminent and worthy citizens, Mr. John Morphew, and Mr. Bernard Lintot.

1749, Henry Fielding, The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling, Dublin: John Smith, Volume 2, Book 8, Chapter 8, pp. 126-127,
This is indeed a most aggravating Circumstance, which attends unjustly depriving Men of their Reputation; for a Man who is Conscious of having an ill Character, cannot justly be angry with those who neglect and slight him; but ought rather to despise those that affect his Conversation, unless where a perfect Intimacy must have convinced them that their Friend’s Character hath been falsely and injuriously aspersed.
If any one had taxed him with the vice, he would have indignantly repelled the accusation, and conceived himself unworthily aspersed.

glosses: Variante de hisopar.
Rociar o echar agua con el hisopo.
Introducir un hisopo en la nariz para obtener una muestra que permita detectar infecciones respiratorias.

glosses: Jeter çà et là des gouttes d’eau ou d’un autre liquide sur quelqu’un ou sur quelque chose.

examples.text: Il faudra asperger le sol avant de passer le coup de balais. Ça fera moins de poussière.

glosses: Projeter, pulvériser un liquide en fines gouttelettes.

examples.text: Face à la vague de chaleur qui terrasse l’Argentine depuis près de deux semaines, une école de Rosario (nord) autorise les enfants à venir en maillot de bain pour pouvoir les asperger à la récréation.

À l’arrivée du grand prix, les vainqueurs, dés leur montée sur le podium, ont secoué des bouteilles de champagne dont ils ont partiellement obturé le goulot avec leur pouce et en ont aspergé le public pour manifester leur joie.
Avant son discours, quinze bouteilles d’eau avaient été alignées devant la table des convives. Était-ce pour asperger nos amis en cas de surchauffe métabolitique?

glosses: Projeter des gouttes de liquide avec un rameau ou un goupillon, lors d’un rite liturgique.

examples.text: On aspergea d’eau bénite les draps du lit.
Un, deux, trois… J’ai aspergé les restes du ténor.

glosses: Se mouiller.
